- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.4) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if true price drops after a spike, forecast should adjust downward by 1–2 periods.
- Reduce forecast magnitude when sentiment declines sharply (e.g., from 0.6 to 0.2) — model overreacts to sentiment drops.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when recent history shows volatility or downward trend — sentiment + price history should constrain forecast range.
- Apply downward bias to 30-day forecasts if sentiment is consistently below 0.5 over last 5 days — model lacks risk-adjustment.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 18-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) — prevent runaway spikes.
